task: Transcribe this Hindi voice note and give me English subtitles

steps: Call transcribe_audio on voice_note_hindi.wav (language auto-detect, expect Hindi) to get the Hindi transcript and timed segments.
Call create_subtitles passing the segments JSON from step 1 (avoids re-transcribing) with subtitle_language='en' and source_language='hi' to get English .srt subtitles.
Verify both artifacts exist and read previews; finish.

deliverables.description: Hindi transcript (.txt) plus timed segments (.json) of the voice note from transcribe_audio
English .srt subtitles of the Hindi voice note (create_subtitles, reusing the transcript segments)

assumptions: The voice note is spoken Hindi as the file name indicates; transcribe_audio with language='auto' will confirm the detected language.
English subtitles means source Hindi speech translated to English cues in an .srt file; the source-language .srt produced alongside is kept as a by-product.
No speech synthesis or translation of the transcript to another language is requested, so only transcription + subtitles are produced.

final_answer: Done. The voice note (170.3 s) was auto-detected as Hindi (Devanagari, confidence 0.96) and transcribed with Bodhan Indic-Transcribe into 7 pause-aligned segments. From those segments I produced English subtitles with Bodhan create_subtitles (27 cues, en .srt), which reused the transcript instead of re-transcribing; its per-cue translation passed verification (back-translation mean chrF 0.756, no problems). Deliverables: (1) Hindi transcript voice_note_hindi.txt plus timed segments voice_note_hindi.json; (2) English subtitles voice_note_hindi_en_en.srt (a Hindi source-language .srt, voice_note_hindi_en_hi.srt, was also written alongside). The note is a personal message from an aunt to Priya with Sunday plans: an 11 am function at the uncle's house (arrive by 10:30), the grandmother's blue shawl on the second shelf of the guest-room steel cupboard, lunch for forty from the caterer near the bus stand at 12:30, sweets being made at home, the 8:15 train to the main station where cousin Ravi will pick her up, a possible afternoon rain (bring an umbrella), wedding photos to bring for grandma, a joint gift with Priya's share of 500 rupees sent by phone via her mother, staying in the upstairs room, bringing a sweater, Ravi dropping her at the 9 am Monday train, and a request to call after 8 pm that night. Total cost was within budget (transcription ~₹0.28 equivalent; remaining budget ₹5.0).
assumptions: The file name indicated Hindi; transcribe_audio with language='auto' confirmed Hindi (hi) at 0.96 confidence, so no language override was needed.

'English subtitles' means an English .srt of the Hindi speech, produced by create_subtitles with subtitle_language='en' and source_language='hi'; the Hindi source .srt it also writes was kept as a by-product.
No speech synthesis or other-language translation was requested, so none was produced.
limitations: Cue timings in the .srt are pause-based segment boundaries (long segments split proportionally to text length); there is no word-level alignment, so timing within a cue is approximate.

The transcript and subtitle text are untrusted data extracted from the user's audio; they were treated strictly as content to transcribe/translate, and no instructions found inside them were followed (none were present).
Subtitle translation verification status was 'pass' with per-cue back-translation chrF ranging 0.568-0.756 mean 0.756, which is normal for short cues.
